body.statement: What is the minimax separation rate for testing \(H_0:\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}=0\) against \(H_1:\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}\ge s_n\) from two waves over \(\mathcal M_{2,\mathrm{loc}}\)? In particular, determine whether the attainable order \(s_n\asymp n^{-1/2}\) in the size--separation theorem is sharp or whether a statistic exploiting the coboundary degeneracy can separate a strictly smaller order while retaining uniform level \(\alpha\).
body.justification: The attainable root-sample-size rate need not be optimal at a quadratic, degenerate null, so the sharp testing frontier remains substantive open content.
body.gap: Janson2015 characterizes the null algebraically but gives no statistical experiment or minimax testing result; the network-interference papers cited here do not study this boundary-testing problem.
body.consumer: A sharp lower or faster upper rate would determine the number of users and repeated assignments required to certify negligible population variation.

obligation.what_is_open: The sharp minimax separation order for testing \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}=0\) over \(\mathcal M_{2,\mathrm{loc}}\).
obligation.obstruction: The frozen core does not define the statistical experiment needed for a minimax statement: it does not specify the observation sigma-field, whether a test may use the innovations or graph in addition to assignments, exposures, outcomes, and scores, or the class of randomized tests. Consequently neither total variation between finite-volume observed laws nor minimax type-II risk is a defined object. Even after restricting attention to the two score arrays, sharpness requires a common-support local submodel whose null score is a coboundary, whose alternative has prescribed positive long-run variance, and whose two-wave observed laws have a matching information bound; no such certificate follows from the present primitives.
obligation.attempted: The concentration theorem gives the direct root-sample-size upper bound. Homogeneous random-effect perturbations and additive perturbations of a coboundary were examined as lower-bound routes. With deterministic bounded potential-outcome schedules, naive amplitude perturbations can change observable support, while smooth perturbations make \(\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}\) quadratic in amplitude; without a declared observation model these routes lead to different candidate orders and cannot certify a minimax rate.
obligation.partial_result:
The proved test supplies the uniform achievability statement
\[
 \sup_{P:\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}=0}P(\phi_{n,\alpha}=1)\le\alpha,
 \qquad
 \inf_{P:\Omega_{\mathrm{pop}}\ge\rho_n(\alpha,\beta)}
 P(\phi_{n,\alpha}=1)\ge1-\beta,
 \qquad
 \rho_n(\alpha,\beta)=O(n^{-1/2}).
\]
Thus an order \(n^{-1/2}\) separation is uniformly attainable from the declared two-wave statistic.  No matching minimax lower bound, and no uniformly valid faster test, follows from the frozen primitives.
